items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4892

SPONSOR: HINCHEY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to the
Nourish New York program

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of the legislation is to create the Nourish NY program
permanently in the Agriculture & Markets Law

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1; - Declaration of Legislative Findings & Intent

   -Creates definitions used in the creation language for the Nourish NY
program
   -Establishes the Nourish NY program as a new Section 452 of the Ag &
Markets Law

Section 2: Effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

While the Nourish New York program was developed in response to
disrupted food supply chains due to the COVID-19 pandemic, it has
emerged as an important innovation, significantly supporting the state's
farms while providing nourishing fresh foods to people experiencing food
insecurity. The COVID-19 crisis unveiled the weaknesses in our state's
food supply system and has caused serious economic hardships for the
state's farms and agribusinesses. But, in the 10 months since its incep-
tion, Nourish New York has already strengthened the state's food supply
network and expanded markets for New York farm products. The local food
movement has also gained significant momentum during the pandemic, with
increasing numbers of New Yorkers wanting to know where their food is
sourced. This presents the state with a major opportunity to support our
local economies and create greater equity in our food system by provid-
ing greater access to local, healthy options in food insecure areas
through making the Nourish New York program permanent.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Legislation

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

TBD.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 45 Chapter 631
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 4892-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to the
        Nourish New York program"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would establish the Nourish New York program in the Agricul-
ture  and  Markets  Law  and require the Commissioner of Agriculture and
Markets to perform a comprehensive review of the Department of  Health's
Hunger Prevention and Nutrition Assistance Program (HPNAP) and study the
need  for a cold storage grant program for food banks and emergency food
providers.
 
  Established in 2020 in response to food supply  chain  issues  arising
from  COVID-19,  the State's Nourish New York program has provided crit-
ical assistance to families and farmers whose lives and livelihoods have
been disrupted by the pandemic. To date, $85 million has been  dedicated
to  the program, supporting New York emergency food service providers in
the purchase of  surplus  products  from  New  York  farmers  and  dairy
manufacturers for families in need across the state.
 
  I  support  the  sponsors' intent to codify this effective program. To
maintain the current program as it exists today, I have  reached  agree-
ment with the Legislature on technical modifications to align the statu-
tory  provisions in this bill with the successful program as established
and administered currently by the Department of Agriculture and Markets.
In addition, the studies required under this bill will  be  led  by  the
Commissioner  of  Health  instead of the Commissioner of Agriculture and
Markets and will be right-sized to effectively provide  the  fundamental
information sought by the studies.

  Based on this agreement, I am pleased to sign this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                           (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                 ______

summary: Establishes the Nourish New York program to facilitate programming that ensures that certain surplus agricultural products are provided to food relief organizations at competitive wholesale prices.
